title: Execute an AGV's Active Command Through the OptiSweep WCS API
summary: Use the OptiSweep / WCS API ExecutedAgvCommand operation with a confirmed robot ID to execute the active command currently held by an AGV. The source describes this as useful after an unplanned restart when OptiSweep missed callbacks from Geek Plus.
when_to_use: Use when an AGV has an active command but OptiSweep missed callbacks from Geek Plus, including the source-described unplanned-restart scenario.
not_for: Do not use without a confirmed robot ID.
Do not use as a replacement-command or manual-command-entry procedure; the source does not define either.
Do not use when the request cannot be submitted or the AGV does not execute its active command without escalating.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support executes the OptiSweep / WCS API request through Apidog or an equivalent WCS API client.
L2_support verifies the AGV result using the available live AGV status or movement view.
L3_support may support escalation when the request cannot be submitted or the active command does not execute.
safety_notes: Use only a confirmed robot ID.
This procedure executes the active command already held by the AGV; it does not define a new command.
access_or_tools_needed: Apidog or equivalent WCS API client
Live AGV status or movement verification

access_required: L2/L3 access to the OptiSweep / WCS API through Apidog or an equivalent WCS API client.
system_preconditions: The AGV has an active command to execute.
A confirmed robot ID is available.

visual_references.description: OptiSweep / WCS API AGVs operation list showing POST Executed Agv Command and the related robot-ID and active-command behavior.
OptiSweep API overview showing Apidog on the primary server and the AGVs API operations.

steps.title: Open the ExecutedAgvCommand operation
steps.purpose: Access the OptiSweep / WCS API operation used to execute the active command held by an AGV.
steps.instruction: In Apidog or an equivalent OptiSweep / WCS API client, open the AGVs API group and locate the operation labeled ExecutedAgvCommand, shown as POST Executed Agv Command.
steps.expected_result: The POST Executed Agv Command operation is available for submission in the OptiSweep / WCS API client.
steps.healthy_condition: The AGVs operation list displays POST Executed Agv Command.
steps.failure_condition: The ExecutedAgvCommand operation is unavailable or the API client cannot be opened.

actions.label: Locate API operation
actions.exact_action: Open the AGVs API operation labeled ExecutedAgvCommand / POST Executed Agv Command.

stop_or_escalate_if: The API client cannot be opened.
The ExecutedAgvCommand operation is not available.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The AGVs API list includes POST Executed Agv Command; ExecutedAgvCommand requires a robot ID and executes the active command the AGV has.
OptiSweep provides APIs for data and requests, and Apidog is installed on the primary servers.

steps.title: Enter the confirmed robot ID
steps.purpose: Target the AGV whose active command is to be executed.
steps.instruction: Provide the confirmed robot ID required by the ExecutedAgvCommand operation in the OptiSweep / WCS API client.
steps.expected_result: The request contains the robot ID for the intended AGV.
steps.healthy_condition: A confirmed robot ID is present for the intended AGV.
steps.failure_condition: The robot ID is missing, unconfirmed, or does not identify the intended AGV.

actions.label: Confirm robot ID
actions.exact_action: Provide the robot ID required by ExecutedAgvCommand.

stop_or_escalate_if: The robot ID cannot be confirmed.
The intended AGV cannot be identified.

steps.title: Submit the active-command request
steps.purpose: Request execution of the active command already held by the AGV.
steps.instruction: Submit the POST ExecutedAgvCommand request in the OptiSweep / WCS API client with the confirmed robot ID.
steps.expected_result: The POST request is submitted for the selected AGV.
steps.healthy_condition: The OptiSweep / WCS API client accepts and submits the POST ExecutedAgvCommand request.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The ExecutedAgvCommand API operation executes the active command held by the AGV and is described as useful during unplanned restarts when OptiSweep missed Geek Plus callbacks.

steps.title: Verify active-command execution
steps.purpose: Confirm on a live AGV surface that the active command was executed.
steps.instruction: Use the live AGV status or movement view, including the OptiSweep / WCS API AGV status information when available, to verify that the selected AGV executes its active command.
steps.expected_result: The selected AGV's live status or movement shows execution or progression of the active command.
steps.healthy_condition: The AGV status or movement view shows the selected AGV executing or progressing the active command.
steps.failure_condition: The AGV does not execute or progress the active command after the request.

actions.label: Verify AGV state
actions.exact_action: Verify on the live AGV status or movement view that the AGV's active command is executed.

stop_or_escalate_if: The AGV does not execute its active command.
The live AGV status or movement view does not show execution or progression.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: ExecutedAgvCommand executes the active command the AGV has.

success_criteria: The POST ExecutedAgvCommand request is submitted with a confirmed robot ID.
The selected AGV executes or progresses its active command on the live AGV status or movement view.
healthy_conditions: The AGVs API group exposes POST Executed Agv Command.
The request contains a confirmed robot ID.
The live AGV status or movement view shows execution or progression of the active command.
failure_conditions: The robot ID is missing or cannot be confirmed.
The AGV does not execute or progress its active command.
escalation_guidance: Escalate to L3_support if the request cannot be submitted.
Escalate to L3_support if the AGV does not execute or progress its active command after the request.
Do not substitute a manually entered or replacement command; no such procedure is provided by the source.
